L'Algérie accélère sa transition vers le: Algeria is accelerating its transition to the IPv6 protocol to address IPv4 address exhaustion and modernize its digital infrastructure. An ambitious plan targets 80% national coverage by 2026, bringing major economic and technological gains.
Le ministère de la Poste et des Télécomm: The Ministry of Post and Telecommunications is launching a massive plan to roll out IPv6 across all 58 wilayas by the end of 2027. This deployment is part of the Digital Plan 2030, with a target of 95% coverage among operators and ISPs by 2028. Pilot tests conducted since 2024 in the wilayas of Algiers, Oran, and Constantine revealed a 30% improvement in latency and a 40% reduction in IP address management costs. The ARPCE has established a strict schedule for operators, including Algérie Télécom, Mobilis SA, Djezzy, and Ooredoo Algérie, featuring a progressive migration of infrastructure.

La transition vers IPv6 répond à des enj: The transition to IPv6 addresses critical challenges for Algeria. With a population exceeding 45 million and a mobile penetration rate of 120% in 2025, the country is facing IPv4 address exhaustion. IPv6 offers a virtually unlimited addressing capacity (2128 addresses), which is essential for developing the Internet of Things (IoT), smart cities, and local cloud services. According to ARPCE, this transition could generate a direct economic gain of 15 billion dinars by 2030, driven by lower management costs and the emergence of new digital services. Technologically, IPv6 improves network security via native encryption mechanisms (IPsec) and reduces the risks of DDoS attacks. For citizens, this translates into better quality of service (QoS) in rural areas, where infrastructure is often limited.
Le calendrier de migration prévoit une p: The migration schedule outlines an initial phase of testing and training until the end of 2026, followed by a massive rollout in 2027. Priority wilayas include Algiers, Oran, Constantine, Annaba, and Tlemcen, where infrastructure experiences the highest demand. The ARPCE will organize regional workshops to raise awareness among local stakeholders, particularly SMEs and public administrations. By 2028, Algeria aims to align its infrastructure with international standards, while already preparing for the arrival of 6G and quantum technologies. A national observatory will be established to monitor network performance, and a digital platform will allow citizens to report connectivity issues. Algérie Télécom has already trained 500 engineers and invested 5 billion dinars in IPv6-compatible equipment.
